evidence.excerpt:
Financial indicators are essential tools for transforming raw finan-
cial data into interpretable measures for various downstream tasks,
such as valuation, risk assessment, and economic analysis. How-
ever, existing financial benchmarks largely focus on answer-level
accuracy and often assume that relevant data are already provided,
leaving the assessment of the intermediate process of indicator con-
struction underexplored. In this work, we proposeFinDeepIndi-
cator, the first benchmark dedicated to evaluating Deep Research
(DR) agents in end-to-end financial indicator construction. Specifi-
cally, FinDeepIndicator evaluates DR agents across four stages in
indicator construction: formula specification, data collection, indi-
cator calculation, and answer generation, and covers fundamental,
technical, and macroeconomic indicators organized into 21 fine-
grained sub-categories. It

evidence.excerpt:
contains 3,350 curated question-answer
(QA) pairs derived from both U.S. and Chinese markets, 10 years
of historical financial data, and 800 listed companies. Extensive
experiments on search-equipped Large Language Models (LLMs)
and DR agents show that, while LLMs generally perform well in
formula specification, their accuracy drops substantially during
data retrieval and numerical execution. DR agents consistently
outperform search-equipped LLMs, yet remain unreliable in realis-
tic financial analysis settings. These findings provide insights for
developing more capable and trustworthy DR agents in finance.

mathematical operations, and relevant domain conventions. The

the Alt-test [2]. Three human experts independently evaluate
the consistency between each parsed formula and the correct

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Human expert inter-annotator agreement (Gwet's AC1) and Alt-test acceptance rates validated both the response parsing and formula evaluation stages against independent human judgments.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: LLM-as-a-judge for semantic formula equivalence, deterministic tolerance-aware cell matching for data and numerical answers against ground-truth tables.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pre-trained and instruction-tuned off-the-shelf LLMs and standard ReAct agent scaffolding evaluated without task-specific training on this benchmark.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding model performance drops between formula understanding and execution, cross-market differences, and data collection bottlenecks are directly supported by tabular and empirical results.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation systematically benchmarks search-equipped LLMs and ReAct-based deep research agents across U.S. and Chinese markets. Process-stage breakdowns, an ablation isolating raw data retrieval, and error analysis validate the central finding that data retrieval is the core performance bottleneck.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Human financial expert evaluations (inter-annotator agreement Gwet's AC1 and Alt-test acceptance) validated both the response parsing and the formula evaluation stages.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: LLM-as-a-judge for semantic formula equivalence, alongside deterministic tolerance-aware cell matching for data and numerical answers against ground-truth tables.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pre-trained and instruction-tuned off-the-shelf LLMs and standard ReAct agent scaffoldings without task-specific training on this benchmark.

primary.limitations: The authors state the scope of public financial/macroeconomic data used, and the text acknowledges model limitations and constraints across technical/macro indicator domains, though a dedicated discussion of benchmark lifespan or live website drift is brief.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly described, detailing the curation of 234 financial indicators, structured template instantiation across three difficulty levels, and a multi-stage evaluation pipeline combining LLM extraction/formula judging with tolerance-aware ground-truth numerical matching.
primary.quality_rationale: The benchmark provides an adequate, structured contribution to evaluating financial research agents beyond simple final-answer QA. Validation of LLM parsing and formula scoring via human inter-annotator agreement and the Alt-test provides sound measurement reliability.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces FinDeepIndicator, an end-to-end benchmarking dataset of 3,350 QA pairs across 234 financial indicators, along with a process-level evaluation framework assessing formula specification, data collection, indicator calculation, and answer generation.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The benchmark provides an adequate, structured contribution to evaluating financial research agents beyond simple final-answer QA. Validation of LLM parsing and formula scoring via human inter-annotator agreement and the Alt-test provides sound measurement reliability.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors state the scope of public financial/macroeconomic data used, and the text acknowledges model limitations and constraints across technical/macro indicator domains, though a dedicated discussion of benchmark lifespan or live website drift is brief.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
